region: Capital and largest city of Angola
heroText: Luanda is Angola's Atlantic capital and main port, an industrial and cultural hub built around a curving bay lined with the Marginal waterfront promenade. First-time visitors should walk the Fortaleza de São Miguel for city and harbour views, cross to Ilha de Luanda for its beaches and seafood shacks, and browse the National Slavery Museum for context on the country's Portuguese-era history. Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport links Luanda to Europe, the Americas and the wider region.

areas.name: Ingombota
areas.text: Ingombota is the central business district holding government offices, banks and many of the capital's top hotels, a practical first-time base.

areas.name: Miramar
areas.text: Miramar is Luanda's upscale seafront district of gated condominiums and international hotels, popular with business travellers for its safety and waterfront access.

areas.name: Maianga
areas.text: Maianga is a quieter, more residential district next to the centre, offering better value stays within easy reach of downtown Luanda.

areas.name: Ilha de Luanda
areas.text: Ilha de Luanda is a narrow sandbar peninsula lined with beach bars and seafood restaurants, best for an evening out rather than an overnight base.

airports.name: Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport (NBJ)
airports.search: Dr. Antonio Agostinho Neto International Airport, Luanda, Angola
airports.text: Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport sits around 40 kilometres southeast of central Luanda; allow extra time for the transfer and confirm hotel pickup in advance.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport (NBJ) and central Luanda before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Ingombota for a central first stay near government offices, banks and hotels, or choose Miramar for gated, upscale waterfront living close to the Marginal. Maianga offers better value for longer stays, while Ilha de Luanda suits an evening of beach bars rather than an overnight base.
hotelIntro: Luanda hotel choice usually comes down to budget and security: Ingombota and Miramar hold the capital's international hotel brands and safest streets, Maianga offers more affordable options close to downtown, and Ilha de Luanda works best as a dinner or nightlife outing rather than a place to sleep.
rentalCars: A rental car is not recommended for visitors, since traffic is heavy and unpredictable; arrange a hotel driver or trusted taxi service instead.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Ingombota or Miramar for a secure first stay close to hotels, restaurants and the Marginal waterfront promenade.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Book a hotel transfer in advance for the 40-kilometre drive from Agostinho Neto International Airport, since taxis are scarce outside arrivals.

travelTips.title: Costs and cash
travelTips.text: Luanda is one of Africa's most expensive cities for visitors, so confirm hotel and taxi prices upfront and carry local kwanza for small purchases.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Set aside a full day for the Kalandula Falls or the Miradouro da Lua rock formations if the itinerary allows time outside the capital.

nearbyIdeas.name: Kalandula Falls
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Kalandula Falls is one of Africa's largest waterfalls, a long but rewarding day trip inland from Luanda through Angola's rural highlands.

nearbyIdeas.name: Miradouro da Lua
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Miradouro da Lua is a striking lunar-like landscape of eroded cliffs south of Luanda, a popular half-day trip along the coast.

history.text: Portuguese colonization Portuguese explorer Paulo Dias de Novais founded Luanda on 25 January 1576 as "São Paulo da Assumpção de Loanda".

history.label: 17th century
history.text: In the 17th century, the Imbangala became the main rivals of the Mbundu in supplying slaves to the Luanda market.
In 1618, the Portuguese built the fortress called Fortaleza São Pedro da Barra, and they subsequently built two more: Fortaleza de São Miguel (1634) and Forte de São Francisco do Penedo (1765–66).
Luanda was Portugal's bridgehead from 1627, except during the Dutch rule of Luanda, from 1640 to 1648, as Fort Aardenburgh.

history.label: 19th century
history.text: In the 19th century, still under Portuguese rule, Luanda experienced a major economic revolution.
A strong degree of Brazilian influence was noted in Luanda until the independence of Brazil in 1822.
The slave trade was abolished in 1836, and in 1844, Angola's ports were opened to foreign shipping.

By 1850, Luanda was one of the greatest and most developed Portuguese cities in the vast Portuguese Empire outside continental Portugal, full of trading companies, exporting (together with Benguela) palm and peanut oil, wax.

history.text: Luanda has been undergoing major road reconstruction in the 21st century, and new highways are planned to improve connections to Cacuaco, Viana, Samba, and the new airport.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: During this period, no large scale territorial conquest was intended by the Portuguese; only a few minor settlements were established in the immediate hinterland of Luanda, some on the last stretch of the Kwanza.
